subject: MedCast SLO handshake: token-burst, streaming slots & canary throughput
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@medcast.ai>, Priyanka Singh <pri.singh@medcast.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: MedCast demo — quick follow-up and performance asks

Hi Anita / Priyanka,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really appreciated the walkthrough of the live transcription flow and the low-latency annotation pipeline. Per our conversation I captured the performance items we need to validate before we can scope a pilot. Attaching the recording for your reference (demo-recording.mp4).

Can you confirm the following in a quick reply? We want to align on measurable SLOs so we can size a canary and produce a runbook.

- Target latency SLOs (P95 preferred) for typical UI responses (short answers) and for long-form outputs (>=512 tokens)
- Expected sustained concurrency (avg sessions concurrently hitting inference) and expected peak bursts (30s-2m)
- Whether streaming is required for all user-facing responses or only for transcription/live captioning flows
- Max input size (tokens) and max output size we should design for (worst case)
- Any hard budget constraints (e.g., cost per active session or monthly inference budget)

Tentative next steps from our side after you confirm: Karthik will propose a canary configuration (model variant + batching + streaming handshake) and an initial cost/latency tradeoff table; Marissa and I will draft a mutual action plan and timeline.

If easier, we can do a 30-min follow-up tomorrow morning — what times work?

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MedCast demo — quick follow-up and performance asks

Thanks Lauren — great session. Quick answers below and I attached our internal performance matrix (medcast-performance-matrix.xlsx) for specifics.

- Latency: For UI micro-interactions (summary lines / label suggestions) we need P95 <= 350ms. For medium outputs (up to ~512 tokens) P95 <= 700ms. For long-form generation (up to 2048 tokens, e.g., stitched clinical notes) we accept P95 up to 1.2s if streaming is used; full non-streamed completion target P95 <= 1.5s.
- Concurrency: Typical sustained concurrency across our pilot cohort is ~60 sessions. Peak bursts occur during shift changes / morning batch-up to ~250 concurrent sessions for 60–120s.
- Streaming: Required for live transcription and for the in-app live draft experience; conversational replies can be non-streaming but must not exceed the medium-output SLOs.
- Token sizes: Inputs are usually short (<=512 tokens), but we need to handle occasional large context windows up to 8192 tokens for full patient context lookups; outputs can be up to 2048 tokens.
- Budget: We have an internal target of keeping inference cost under $0.12 per active session during pilot. Procurement looped in for contracts.

We'd like Redwood to propose a canary that demonstrates both latency compliance and graceful degradation during the 200–300 concurrent burst.

Thanks,
Anita Rao
Head of Product, MedCast Health
anita@medcast.ai

Subject: Internal: MedCast SLOs — propose canary options

Karthik / Marissa — Anita sent the numbers above (P95 targets, concurrency, large context up to 8k tokens). Important constraints:

- P95 <= 350ms (short), <=700ms (<=512 tokens), up to ~1.2s when streaming for very long outputs
- Sustained 60 concurrent users, predictable bursts to 250 for ~1–2 minutes
- Must support streaming for transcription and keep cost <= $0.12/active-session during pilot

Ask: please draft two canary options by EOD Pacific today:
1) Low-latency canary (priority latency): target P95 headroom with reserved capacity, aggressive batching disabled for streaming flows, fallback to smaller quantized model for non-critical outputs. Include expected cost per active session.
2) Cost-optimized canary (priority cost): use smart batching for non-streaming flows, prefix KV caching for repeated prompts, and a hybrid routing policy (hosted low-latency pool for streaming + cheaper burst pool for non-streaming). Include expected P95 degradation under 250 concurrency bursts.

Key technical notes for the sizing doc:
- For 8k token context, we should measure KV cache RAM needs and incremental latency; prefer to avoid decompressing full context on every request.
- For streaming handshake we should use chunked responses with early tokens emitted as soon as they're available (do not block on full decode).
- For burst hedging, propose automatic fallback to a smaller model family with graceful truncation/notice in UI.

I will coordinate the follow-up with Anita for Wed 10am PT to review canary choices — confirm availability.

Thanks —
Lauren

Lauren / team — initial sizing notes and recommendations (high level). I attached a short PDF with the numbers (sizing-estimates.pdf).

Summary:
- Baseline config (low-latency): 1x model shard with optimized kernels (FP16 quantized where feasible), dedicated GPU pool for streaming. Expected P95: ~280–340ms for short messages (<=128 tokens). For 512-token responses P95 ~ 600–750ms (depends on decoding strategy), for streaming long outputs we can hit 1.0–1.1s P95 for emitted tokens; full completion will be higher but within Anita's tolerance if streamed.
- Concurrency handling: a reserved pool sized for sustained 70 concurrency with burst autoscale to 320 using a warm standby pool. Autoscale delta should be governed by a 30–60s smoothing window to avoid flapping.
- Cost estimates: low-latency reserved setup ~ $0.10–0.14 per active session (depends on traffic profile and average generated tokens). Cost-optimized hybrid setup ~ $0.06–0.09 per active session with batching + small-model fallbacks.
- 8k context: recommend an LRU KV cache per-client for patient context; keep hot patient contexts pinned to RAM for the canary cohort to avoid a cold-load penalty. Measure memory: ~1.2GB per 100 pinned contexts for quantized embeddings; we should budget accordingly.
- Streaming handshake: use chunked SSE/WebSocket output with first-byte emission on prefix decode (i.e., do not wait for full beam). This reduces perceived latency but requires per-client streaming slots in the pool. Suggest an initial streaming slot ratio of 1:3 (streaming slots : non-streaming slots) for pilot.

Next actions: I'll convert these into two explicit config YAMLs (low-latency vs cost-optimized) and include measured latency curves from our internal bench. Can have that ready by EOD and present at Wed 10am PT.
